name: Normandy landings

phases.title: Airborne troops land behind the beaches
phases.text: Pathfinders of the US airborne divisions arrived at 00:15, and British glider troops took the Caen canal and Orne bridges at 00:16. Many paratroopers landed far from their drop zones.

phases.title: The flanks are taken
phases.text: On the western side the 82nd Airborne captured the crossroads at Sainte-Mère-Église within two hours of landing. On the eastern side the 6th Airborne held the bridges over the Caen canal and the Orne.

phases.title: The fleet shells the coast
phases.text: Warships bombarded the ground behind the beaches in the dark and, from 05:50, pre-assigned targets on the beaches themselves. The assault divisions crossed in landing craft, which strong winds blew east of their intended positions.

phases.title: Utah and Omaha are landed on
phases.text: The 8th Infantry Regiment of the 4th Division landed first at Utah at 06:30, about 1,800 metres south of its intended place. At Omaha, where the 1st and 29th Divisions came ashore, obstacles were largely undamaged and fire from the cliffs was heavy.

phases.title: Gold, Sword and Juno are landed on
phases.text: Landings at Gold were set for 07:25 and infantry began disembarking at Sword at 07:30. At Juno the landing was delayed by choppy seas, and the men arrived ahead of their supporting armour and suffered many casualties.

phases.title: Combat teams leave Utah Beach
phases.text: Combat teams began to leave Utah at around 09:00, some infantry wading through flooded fields. They skirmished with the 919th Grenadier Regiment through the day, and the 4th Division made a rendezvous with the airborne troops.

phases.title: Barely 600 men reach the heights at Omaha
phases.text: Exit from Omaha was possible only through five heavily defended gullies, and by late morning barely 600 men had reached the higher ground. By noon the Americans were able to clear some lanes on the beaches.

phases.title: Fortified towns are cleared at Gold, Juno and Sword
phases.text: At Gold, Juno and Sword the fortified towns were cleared in house-to-house fighting. The 2nd Battalion, King's Shropshire Light Infantry advanced on Caen to within a few kilometres of the town but had to withdraw for lack of armour support.

phases.title: The 21st Panzer Division counter-attacks
phases.text: The 21st Panzer Division attacked between Sword and Juno and nearly reached the Channel. It met stiff resistance from the British 3rd Division and was soon recalled to the area between Caen and Bayeux.

note: The plan shows the whole operation of 6 June 1944, not a single field: the blocks are fleets, divisions and airborne forces. The accounts give the sectors in order from west to east (Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno, Sword) but not distances, so the places of the beaches, towns and German units are set by judgement. Pointe du Hoc and the French Resistance's sabotage are left off the plan.
